points: Selective photothermolysis: melanin and oxyhaemoglobin absorb the light and heat up; dermal heating may remodel collagen modestly.
Darker or tanned skin absorbs more epidermal energy, giving a higher risk of burns and pigment change.
Sessions often 3–6, weeks apart; treated pigment darkens like “coffee grounds” then flakes over 1–2 weeks.
Adverse effects: burns, blistering, **hypo-/hyperpigmentation** (sometimes grid footprints), scarring, paradoxical hair growth, eye injury.

cards.name: Diffuse redness + lentigines
cards.clue: IPL photofacial after a skin cancer check

cards.name: Discrete stubborn lentigo
cards.clue: Often a pigment laser rather than IPL

cards.name: Melasma
cards.clue: Sunscreen + medical therapy; avoid heat devices first-line (see [Melasma](condition:melasma-facial-melanosis))

items.t: Eye pain or visual change during/after IPL: **urgent ophthalmology**.
Blistering burns or striped hypopigmentation: stop further treatment; specialist wound/pigment advice.
Undiagnosed changing pigmented lesion: cancel IPL; refer.

pearls.t: IPL is versatile but unforgiving on tanned or darker skin without expert settings.
Coffee-ground darkening is expected; picking prolongs marks.

quiz.q: Name a red flag that needs escalation.
quiz.a: Eye pain or visual change during/after IPL: **urgent ophthalmology**.
